summary: South Africa admits most Western passports visa-free — 90 days for the US, UK, most of Western Europe, Japan, Brazil and Russia, and 30 days for several others — while nationalities such as China and India need a visa from a South African mission (with an eVisa scheme being rolled out for some). Two fully blank passport pages are strictly required at the border.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 30 days after your intended departure from South Africa — though at least 6 months' validity is recommended, since airlines and neighbouring countries often apply stricter standards.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required if you arrive from, or transited more than 12 hours through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — this catches many itineraries routed through African hubs such as Nairobi or Addis Ababa.

source.name: South African Government (gov.za)

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical cover is strongly recommended — South Africa's excellent private hospitals require payment guarantees, and public hospitals are under strain.

source.name: South African Government (gov.za)

onwardTicket.text: Visitors must be able to show a return or onward ticket; airlines check this at check-in and immigration officers may ask again on arrival.

source.name: Department of Home Affairs — Types of Visas

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must have sufficient funds for their stay; there is no published fixed amount, but immigration officers can ask for bank statements or cash and cards as evidence.

source.name: Department of Home Affairs — Types of Visas

currencyLimits.text: Travellers may carry at most 25,000 ZAR in South African banknotes in or out; foreign currency of more than 10,000 USD equivalent must be declared to customs.

source.name: South African Government (gov.za)

notes: Children under 18 should travel with an unabridged (full) birth certificate; the rules for foreign minors were relaxed in 2019 but officials still recommend carrying one, and it remains required in some cases (e.g. a child travelling with one parent or unaccompanied).
Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes and 2 litres of wine plus 1 litre of spirits per adult.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments are accepted almost everywhere, including supermarkets, fuel stations and restaurants. Keep a little cash for informal markets, car guards and tips, but you can run most of a trip on a card.

safety.text: South Africa has high crime rates, but millions of tourists visit safely each year by managing risk: use Uber/Bolt or hotel transfers rather than walking at night, keep valuables out of sight, keep car doors locked and windows up in cities (smash-and-grab and carjacking occur at intersections), and stick to well-travelled areas — ask locals which neighbourhoods to avoid.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — South Africa Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to September (the dry southern-hemisphere winter) is the best time for safari in Kruger — thin bush and animals at waterholes. For Cape Town and the Garden Route, the warm, dry summer from November to March is ideal.

idp.text: South Africa is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognises an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: South Africa is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognises an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national licence, and for how long a foreign licence may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for South Africa yet.

tips.text: South Africa strictly enforces the rule of two fully blank visa pages in your passport — airlines refuse boarding and immigration can refuse entry without them. Check your passport before booking.

Travelling with children? Carry each child's unabridged (full) birth certificate and, if one parent is absent, a consent affidavit. The strict 2015-era rules were relaxed for foreign tourists, but officials still ask in edge cases.
Self-driving is the best way to see South Africa — just keep doors locked and bags in the boot, leave space to pull out at traffic lights at night, and never leave anything visible in a parked car.
Tap water is safe to drink in Cape Town, Johannesburg and other major cities. In rural areas, townships with intermittent supply, and after storms, stick to bottled or filtered water.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for South Africa?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders get a free visitor's permit on arrival for stays of up to 90 days. You do need a passport valid for 30 days beyond departure with two fully blank visa pages, and a return or onward ticket.

faq.question: How many blank passport pages does South Africa require?
faq.answer: Two fully blank visa pages, and the rule is strictly enforced — airlines deny boarding and immigration can turn you away if your passport is full. If you are short on pages, renew your passport before the trip.

faq.question: What documents do children need to enter South Africa?
faq.answer: Foreign visa-exempt minors no longer must present a birth certificate since the 2019 relaxation, but Home Affairs still recommends carrying the child's unabridged birth certificate, and it is required in specific cases — a child travelling with one parent should also carry consent from the other. Check the Department of Home Affairs guidance before flying with kids.

faq.question: Do Chinese and Indian citizens need a visa for South Africa?
faq.answer: Yes. Both need a visitor's visa, traditionally issued through South African missions and their visa contractors. South Africa has been rolling out an eVisa for selected nationalities including China and India — check the Department of Home Affairs website (dha.gov.za) for whether the online channel is currently open for your country.

faq.question: Is South Africa safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Millions visit safely every year, but crime is a real risk that you manage rather than ignore: use ride-hailing apps or transfers instead of walking after dark, keep phones and cameras out of sight on the street, keep car doors locked with windows up in cities, and get local advice on which areas to avoid. Safari areas, wine regions and the main tourist routes are generally relaxed.
